name: Law firms (operations and admin)

problems.words: We missed a hearing because the date was only in the munshi's diary
quick_ideas: Copy the next month's hearing dates once into a shared calendar with the responsible lawyer named, so the diary is no longer the only copy
Name a backup clerk for when the munshi is away, so dates keep being updated.

workzap_build.text: a shared hearing diary by matter that the clerk updates from his phone after each hearing, with a morning WhatsApp summary of today's and tomorrow's dates to every lawyer.

problems.ask_first: Is the diary kept on paper, or already in a sheet?
problems.free_stops: how adjournments are captured and who receives which alerts are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many upcoming hearing dates sit only in one diary today, so you see the risk tied to one notebook.
Write all upcoming hearing dates in one office register before closing daily, so court attendance stops relying on one person's diary.

problems.words: The cause list is checked by hand every evening
quick_ideas: Make one list of active matters grouped by court, so the evening check is against a fixed list rather than memory
Give the check to one named person at a fixed time, so it is never skipped.

workzap_build.text: an evening routine that lists the firm's active matters by court for the clerk to tick off, records that the check was done, and sends any matter fixed for tomorrow to the responsible lawyer.

problems.ask_first: Is the evening check mostly about one court, or several different courts each day?
problems.free_stops: how the list is kept current and how results reach lawyers are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how long the evening cause list check takes across one week, so you see where admin time is being absorbed.
Keep one handwritten court-wise matters list beside the checker each evening, so the review stays quick and consistent.

problems.words: Physical files go missing between chambers and court
quick_ideas: Start a simple out-and-in register for files at reception, so you know who took a file and when
Do one shelf count of active files, so you know what is missing today.

workzap_build.text: a file check-out and check-in log on phone showing who holds each physical file and since when, flagging files that went to court and haven't come back.

problems.ask_first: Do files go missing mostly on the way to court, or after coming back to chambers?
problems.free_stops: the labelling and check-in routine are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the files expected back from court with the files actually on shelves tonight, so missing movement stands out immediately.
Make one return point for all files coming back from court each day, so chambers always knows where to look next.

problems.words: Clients keep calling to ask what happened at the last hearing
quick_ideas: Agree that the lawyer sends a short update after each hearing this week, so clients stop needing to call
Tell clients once when they can expect updates, so calls drop.

workzap_build.text: a post-hearing note drafted from the diary entry and sent to the client by WhatsApp once the lawyer approves it.

problems.ask_first: Do most calls come from a few clients, or from nearly every client after each hearing?
problems.free_stops: the approval step and message format are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many calls ask about the last hearing this week, so you see which matters are creating repeat interruptions.
Give one staff member the job of noting post-hearing updates in one client call list daily, so callers get timely answers.

problems.words: Associates' time is never recorded, so we underbill
quick_ideas: Ask associates to note time on fixed-fee matters for one month, so you see which ones are losing money
Compare that once against the fee agreed, so the worst matters stand out.

workzap_build.text: simple time capture per matter rolled up daily into fee versus effort, with fixed-fee matters flagged as they run over.

problems.ask_first: Do all lawyers skip recording time, or mainly the juniors on fixed-fee work?
problems.free_stops: how time is captured and how matters are compared are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count once this week how many workdays end without any associate notes on tasks done, so missing effort stops being invisible.
Give one admin person a single end of day check for task notes from each associate, so billing discussions start from complete records.

problems.words: Clients pay the first instalment then disappear, and court fees we paid never come back
quick_ideas: List once, per matter, the fee agreed, what has been paid and what you spent on the client's behalf, so the real balance is clear
Send each client with a balance one statement this week, so the amount is in front of them.

workzap_build.text: a balance per matter that includes court fees and disbursements, adds them to invoices automatically and sends reminders on schedule.

problems.ask_first: Do clients vanish mostly on a few matter types, or on all kinds of cases?
problems.free_stops: how expenses are logged and the reminder sequence are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count once this week how many matters have firm-paid expenses noted without any matching recovery note, so the backlog size is clear.
Give one staff member a fixed weekly review of firm-paid expense notes in one notebook, so follow-up stops slipping between desks.

problems.words: Drafts go back and forth on WhatsApp and we lose the final version
quick_ideas: Create one folder per active matter and move current drafts there, so the latest version has one home
Mark the final version clearly once it is agreed, so nobody works from an old copy.

workzap_build.text: a template and draft register per matter with version history, so every draft is saved in one place and the final is locked.

problems.ask_first: Do drafts go missing mostly with a few lawyers, or across the whole firm?
problems.free_stops: the template library and versioning rules are designed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many active matters have more than one draft marked final today, so the confusion is clear at a glance.
Choose one office location for the current final draft of each matter, so everyone checks the same place before editing.

problems.words: Limitation dates and filing deadlines are tracked in someone's head
quick_ideas: Walk through all active matter files once and note every unwritten deadline in one notebook, so urgent exposure shows today.
Assign one staff member to update one central deadlines register before closing daily, so key dates stop living in memory.

workzap_build.text: a deadline tracker with escalating alerts to the responsible lawyer and then the partner as each date approaches.

problems.ask_first: Have you missed a date before, or has it only been a close call so far?
problems.free_stops: the escalation steps and timings are kept for the solution document.
quick_ideas_original: Add a deadline column to your matter list and fill it once for every active matter, so dates are written down
Review that column with the partners once, so nothing urgent is hidden.

problems.words: Leads from our website just sit in an inbox
quick_ideas: Go through the inbox once and reply to every unanswered enquiry, so no warm lead is wasted
Name one person who owns new enquiries, so replies stop depending on who looks.

workzap_build.text: every enquiry from the website, phone and WhatsApp recorded, assigned and followed up on time, with the source noted so you see which channels bring paying clients.

problems.ask_first: Do leads sit because nobody checks the inbox, or because nobody knows whose job it is?
problems.free_stops: the assignment rules and follow-up timings are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count unanswered website enquiries sitting since earlier this week, so you see how much potential work is waiting.
Give one person the inbox check at the same time each day, so new enquiries get a clear owner immediately.

never_say: Any legal view, comment on a case's merits, strategy or likely outcome.
Any interpretation of law, court procedure or limitation rules.
Anything touching backdating, forged documents or influencing courts, police or officials.
Regulatory advice on trust or client accounts.
That hearings will never be missed again.
Requests for client names, opposing parties, case numbers or case facts.

sample_reply.person: Dates are our biggest problem. Everything is in the munshi's diary and we've missed hearings when he's away. Can you suggest a fix?
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, you can start on this now, and the first steps are simple.
First, copy the next month of hearing dates once into a shared calendar with the responsible lawyer named on each, so the diary is no longer the only copy.
Second, name a backup clerk for when the munshi is on leave, so dates keep being updated.
On top of this, Workzap could arrange: a shared diary the clerk updates from his phone after every hearing, with a morning summary to each lawyer.

Would you like me to put together a solution document and quote for you? You're free to say no.
